findings.title: All 12 functional success criteria are mapped to specific tasks
findings.description: Cross-reference verified: SC1 (present metrics) → Tasks 8/9 + 12-15; SC2 (function set parity) → Task 9; SC3 (known fixture values) → Tasks 4 + 6; SC4 (duplication boundaries + cross-language) → Tasks 11 + 15; SC5 (absence reasons with details) → Task 22; SC6 (coverage.py totals + tool_ignored_files) → Tasks 20 + 24; SC7 (Istanbul version 0.1 + provider limit text) → Tasks 20 + 24; SC8 (malformed/no-version reports) → Task 20; SC9 (preflight rejects bad paths) → Task 17; SC10 (DUPLICATION_MAX_TOKENS trigger) → Task 11; SC11 (read-only + determinism) → Task 26; SC12 (400 length values unchanged) → Task 7. Each criterion is explicitly cited in the task that proves it.

findings.title: Technical and Integration Requirements covered
findings.description: Ruff/pyright/format are required in every task's Success block and re-validated in Task 30. The ~300-line module limit is enforced in Tasks 10/12/14 (with the contingency to extract into `python_tokens.py`/`typescript_tokens.py`) and re-checked in Task 30. Real Cobertura reports (coverage.py + Istanbul) are captured as fixtures in Task 18 and consumed by Task 20, satisfying the parsing-rule clause. Failure-mode rows from the Data Flow table are exercised by Tasks 9, 11, 13, 15, 20, 22 (signal + outcome). The "enum members only" diff is verified by Task 30's `git diff` check, and `take.py`/`contract.py`/`files.py`/`store.py` no-diff is asserted there.

findings.title: Test-with pattern consistently followed
findings.description: Every implementation task is immediately followed by its test task: Task 3 → 4 (Python complexity), Task 5 → 6 (TypeScript complexity), Task 8 → 9 (complexity integration), Task 10 → 11 (duplication core), Task 12 → 13 (Python duplication), Task 14 → 15 (TypeScript duplication), Task 16 → 17 (config + preflight), Task 19 → 20 (reader), Task 21 → 22 (freshness), Task 23 → 24 (per-language measurements), Task 25 → 26 (adapter wiring), Task 27 carries its own `test_render.py` checks.

findings.title: Sequencing respects dependencies; no cycles
findings.description: The order matches the slice design's Development Approach (enums → complexity walks → duplication → coverage key → reader → freshness → measurements → adapter wiring → render → docs → walkthrough). Task 2 explicitly narrows `PythonAdapter.metrics` to the four 400 metrics so `take_snapshot` doesn't raise on the new enum members before they're measured (later tasks add each metric as it's wired). Task 7's read-and-decode helper is required by Task 10 (duplication). Cobertura parsing (Task 19) precedes freshness (Task 21) and per-language measurements (Task 23).

findings.title: Commit markers sit at working, tested points
findings.description: 17 commits land at logical units: after each test task (Tasks 4, 6, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 20, 22, 24, 26), after the refactor (Task 7), the render task (Task 27), and the docs/walkthrough (Tasks 28, 29). Structural work without their own marker (Tasks 1, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 19, 21, 23, 25) is folded into the next task's commit, which matches the working-tested pattern. Task 30 captures "any remaining changes". No commits at the file end only.

findings.title: Task granularity proportional to slice scope
findings.description: 30 tasks with declared Effort totaling ~60 units for a slice that adds four metrics across two languages plus a Cobertura reader, freshness check, and walkthrough. Largest single task is the duplication core (Task 10, Effort 4) which is a coherent unit (single module, single pass). No task fragments a single decision across multiple tasks, and no task bundles distinct decisions. 30 is in line with the slice's breadth (4 metrics × 2 languages + reader + freshness + walkthrough).

findings.title: Junior-AI completability
findings.description: Each task names the file(s) to change, lists the exact behavior with examples (e.g., the SC3 fixtures with their expected scores of 6, the D2/D3 decision-point lists, the D6 path-validity rule with the bad-input set), and ends with a concrete Success criterion (test pass, ruff/pyright clean, specific invariant). Citations to decisions (D1–D6) and slice-design sections (Data Flow failure-mode table, API Contracts example) keep the task self-contained without restating the design.

findings.title: No scope creep beyond success criteria
findings.description: Every task traces back to either a Functional/Technical/Integration requirement or to the Verification Walkthrough (Task 29). No tasks propose new metrics, additional languages, additional coverage formats, or follow-on work listed under the slice design's Excluded section. The `gitignored` clause for the coverage report is referenced where Task 22 needs it, not invented.

findings.title: No load test task needed
findings.description: The slice design does not restate an NFR that would require a load test. Duplication's memory ceiling (`DUPLICATION_MAX_TOKENS = 4_000_000`) is enforced in software by Task 10 and tested in Task 11 via `monkeypatch`. No CI wiring task is needed because there is no load test to gate on.
